description: The mathematics that computer science is written in: logic, proof, sets, relations, counting, number theory and graphs, taught by proving and computing rather than memorising. Taught to the depth of the standard mathematics-for-computer-science course, with every proof technique practised on real problems.
modelledOn: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
Lehman, Leighton and Meyer, Mathematics for Computer Science
outcomes: Translate English statements into propositional and predicate logic and check validity with truth tables and inference rules.
Write correct proofs by direct argument, contrapositive, contradiction, cases and induction, including strong and structural induction.
Work fluently with sets, functions and relations, and prove properties such as injectivity, equivalence and partial order.
Count arrangements with permutations, combinations, the pigeonhole principle and inclusion-exclusion, and solve recurrences.
Apply modular arithmetic, GCD and the Chinese remainder theorem, including to RSA.
Model problems as graphs and reason about paths, trees, colourings and planarity.

units.title: Propositional and predicate logic
topics: Propositions, connectives, truth tables, tautologies and contradictions
Logical equivalence, De Morgan's laws, conditional and biconditional, converse and contrapositive
Rules of inference: modus ponens, modus tollens, resolution; valid and invalid arguments
Predicates and quantifiers; nested quantifiers; negating quantified statements
Normal forms (CNF, DNF) and satisfiability; logic puzzles

units.title: Proof techniques
topics: Axioms, definitions, theorems, lemmas; what a proof is and is not
Direct proof, proof by contrapositive, proof by contradiction, proof by cases
Existence and uniqueness proofs; counterexamples
Common errors: circular reasoning, proving the converse, division by zero
Proof that the square root of 2 is irrational; infinitude of primes

units.title: Sets, functions and relations
topics: Set notation, subsets, power sets, Cartesian products; set operations and identities; Venn diagrams
Binary operations on sets; closure, associativity, commutativity, identity and inverse
Functions: domain, codomain, image; injective, surjective, bijective; composition and inverse
Relations: reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric, transitive; equivalence relations and partitions
Partial orders, Hasse diagrams, lattices; closures of relations
Cardinality: countable and uncountable sets, Cantor's diagonal argument

units.title: Number systems and number theory
topics: Integers, rationals, reals; positional number systems and base conversion
Divisibility, primes, the fundamental theorem of arithmetic
The division algorithm, Euclid's algorithm, extended Euclid and Bezout's identity
Modular arithmetic, congruences, inverses mod n; Fermat's little theorem and Euler's theorem
Chinese remainder theorem; RSA encryption as an application
Representing integers and floating-point numbers in a computer

units.title: Sequences, series, induction and recursion
topics: Sequences and summation notation; arithmetic and geometric series; telescoping sums
Weak and strong induction; well-ordering principle; common induction mistakes
Recursive definitions of sequences, sets and functions; structural induction
Solving linear recurrences: characteristic equations, Fibonacci closed form
Recursive algorithms and proving them correct; towers of Hanoi, merge sort recurrence
Asymptotic notation: big-O, big-Omega, big-Theta

units.title: Counting and combinatorics
topics: Sum and product rules; permutations and combinations; binomial theorem and Pascal's triangle
Pigeonhole principle and its generalisation
Inclusion-exclusion; derangements
Counting with repetition; stars and bars; distributing objects into boxes
Introduction to discrete probability: sample spaces, events, conditional probability

units.title: Boolean algebra
topics: Boolean algebra as a mathematical structure; axioms and duality
Boolean functions, truth tables, sum-of-products and product-of-sums expressions
Simplification with identities and Karnaugh maps
Logic gates and circuits as Boolean expressions; functional completeness of NAND
Boolean algebra and set algebra as the same lattice

units.title: Graph theory
topics: Graphs, digraphs, multigraphs; degree, handshaking lemma; adjacency matrix and list
Paths, cycles, connectivity, components; Euler circuits and Hamiltonian cycles
Trees, spanning trees, rooted trees; properties and counting of trees
Shortest paths with Dijkstra; minimum spanning trees with Kruskal and Prim
Graph colouring, chromatic number, bipartite graphs and matching
Planar graphs and Euler's formula; modelling road networks and timetables as graphs

schedule.title: Propositional logic and inference
schedule.exercise: Show with truth tables that an implication equals its contrapositive but not its converse. Then test three short arguments for validity.

tasks.title: Build the truth table of (p implies q) and (q implies r) for all 8 rows and classify the formula as tautology, contradiction or contingent
Use the logic tool to show that three pairs of formulas obey De Morgan's laws and conditional equivalences, checking every row
Decide validity of five arguments in propositional form with a truth table, identify the rule behind each valid one and find a counterexample to the invalid ones

schedule.title: Quantifiers and normal forms
schedule.exercise: Negate four nested quantified statements about a student database and say which variable order changes the meaning.

tasks.title: Evaluate 'for every x there exists y with x + y = 0' over the integers 0 to 5 and over a small finite set, and negate it correctly
Convert a four-variable formula to CNF and DNF by tabulating its truth table and confirm both forms agree on all 16 rows
Encode a 5-person seating or knights-and-knaves puzzle as propositional clauses, test all assignments and report the unique solution

schedule.title: Proof techniques
schedule.exercise: Write full proofs of three statements by direct, contrapositive and contradiction methods, and spot the flaw in a given false proof.

tasks.title: Search integers 1 to 100 for counterexamples to 'n squared plus n plus 41 is prime' and report the first one found
Check by computer that the sum of two odd integers is even for 1000 pairs, then write the algebraic proof that it holds for all
Examine a flawed proof that 1 equals 2 via division by zero, locate the invalid step with a numeric check and write a corrected argument

schedule.title: Sets, operations and functions
schedule.exercise: Prove one set identity with element-wise reasoning and verify it with a Venn diagram. Classify five functions as injective, surjective or bijective.

tasks.title: List the power set of {a, b, c, d}, count its 16 elements and compute A union B, A intersect B and A minus B for two given sets
Test closure, associativity, identity and inverses of addition mod 6 and multiplication mod 6 on the integers 0 to 5 using tables
Classify five functions on finite domains as injective, surjective or bijective, compose two of them and compute inverses where they exist

schedule.title: Relations, orders and infinity
schedule.exercise: Show that congruence mod 5 is an equivalence relation and list its classes. Explain Cantor's diagonal argument in your own words.

tasks.title: Test a relation matrix on 5 elements for reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric and transitive properties and state which hold
Draw the Hasse diagram of divisibility on the numbers 1 to 12, find maximal, minimal and the greatest lower bound of 4 and 6
Compute the reflexive, symmetric and transitive closures of a relation on 6 elements with Warshall's algorithm and verify each against its definition

schedule.title: Number theory foundations
schedule.exercise: Run Euclid's algorithm by hand on two three-digit numbers, then back-substitute to express the gcd as a combination.

tasks.title: Convert five decimal numbers to binary, octal and base 7 and convert two back, checking each result by evaluating the digits
Factor ten integers between 100 and 1000 into primes with a sieve and verify the factorisation multiplies back to the original
Run the extended Euclidean algorithm on 5 pairs to find Bezout coefficients and use them to solve linear Diophantine equations

schedule.title: Modular arithmetic and RSA
schedule.exercise: Find the inverse of 7 mod 40 by hand and use it to decrypt a short RSA message built from tiny primes.

tasks.title: Compute a modular inverse table for mod 11 and verify Fermat's little theorem for a = 2, 3 and 5
Solve a system of three congruences with the Chinese remainder theorem and confirm the answer against each modulus
Generate an RSA key pair from two primes below 100, encrypt and decrypt a short message and then factor the modulus to break it

schedule.title: Sums, induction and recursion
schedule.exercise: Prove that the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared by induction, then spot the error in a flawed induction proof.

tasks.title: Evaluate arithmetic and geometric series for 10 terms using formulas, compare with direct sums and verify a telescoping sum numerically
Check an induction claim numerically for n up to 50, then write the base and inductive steps for it as a formal proof
Define a set of balanced bracket strings recursively, generate all strings up to length 8 and verify a structural induction property on each

schedule.title: Recurrences and growth rates
schedule.exercise: Solve a second-order linear recurrence with its characteristic equation and compare the closed form with the first ten terms.

tasks.title: Compute the first 20 Fibonacci numbers and compare them with Binet's closed form, reporting the maximum rounding error
Step through towers of Hanoi for 4 disks and merge sort on 8 numbers, count moves and comparisons and match them to their recurrences
Plot five functions such as n log n, n squared and 2 to the n on log axes and find the crossover points that justify their big-O ordering

schedule.title: Counting and probability
schedule.exercise: Count the arrangements of the letters in a word with repeats, then compute the chance a random mobile money PIN has no repeated digit.

tasks.title: Compute permutations and combinations for five small cases and show the binomial coefficients in rows 0 to 8 of Pascal's triangle
Count the integers from 1 to 1000 divisible by 3, 5 or 7 using inclusion-exclusion and confirm by brute-force enumeration
Estimate the probability two of 30 students share a birthday by Monte Carlo with 10000 trials and compare it with the exact count

schedule.title: Boolean algebra and logic circuits
schedule.exercise: Simplify a four-variable function with a Karnaugh map, draw the gate circuit and show that NAND alone can build it.

tasks.title: Write the truth table for a 3-input majority function and derive its sum-of-products and product-of-sums expressions
Minimise a 4-variable function with a Karnaugh map, list the prime implicants and check the result against the truth table
Build the minimised function using only NAND gates on the circuit bench and verify all 16 input combinations against the truth table

schedule.title: Graph basics, paths and trees
schedule.exercise: Prove the handshaking lemma and use it to show no graph has exactly one odd-degree vertex. Decide whether given graphs have Euler circuits.

tasks.title: Build the adjacency matrix and list of a 6-vertex graph, compute all degrees and verify the handshaking lemma
Test five graphs for Euler circuits by degree rule and find one by hand, then check connectivity and count components
Count the spanning trees of a small graph with the matrix-tree theorem and confirm the count by enumerating them

schedule.title: Graph algorithms and modelling
schedule.exercise: Model a small town's roads and a school timetable as graphs and state what shortest path, spanning tree and colouring mean for each.

tasks.title: Step through Dijkstra on an 8-vertex road network, record the distance table after each step and read off the shortest route
Build a minimum spanning tree of a 7-vertex network with both Kruskal and Prim, and show they give the same total weight
Colour the conflict graph of a school exam timetable with the fewest slots, prove the chromatic number and check planarity with Euler's formula
